title: Gabe Ikard: Oklahoma's First Wuerffel Trophy Winner
question: Which Oklahoma center won the 2013 Wuerffel Trophy?
answer: Gabe Ikard, the Sooners' center from Oklahoma City, won the Wuerffel Trophy for the 2013 season, becoming the first Oklahoma winner of the award for community service paired with academic and athletic excellence.
summary: Gabe Ikard, OU's 2013 All-American center, earned the Wuerffel Trophy for service, a 4.0 GPA and a Sugar Bowl upset of Alabama.
body: Most Oklahoma trophy stories are about touchdowns and tackles. Gabe Ikard's is about a center who also became one of the most decorated students in program history. The Wuerffel Trophy honors the FBS player who best combines community service with academic and athletic achievement, and Ikard's 2013 season earned it for the Sooners for the first time.

On the field, the Oklahoma City native began as a highly recruited tight end prospect, moved to the offensive line, and settled in as the anchor at center. The Wuerffel Foundation reports that he never allowed a sack in 2013, a year that ended 11-2 with a 45-31 Sugar Bowl upset of Alabama and a No. 6 final ranking. CBS Sports, Walter Camp and the AFCA each named him first-team All-American.

The classroom résumé is just as striking. Ikard finished his bachelor's degree in multidisciplinary studies with a 4.0 GPA, was Academic All-Big 12 first team all four years, and was named the Academic All-American of the Year as a senior. He was also the first Sooner football player to be a three-time Academic All-American.

Away from the stadium, he served on OU's Fellowship of Christian Athletes leadership team, joined teammates on a 2012 trip to Haiti to help rebuild after the 2010 earthquake, and volunteered after the deadly Oklahoma tornadoes in May 2013. He was also a finalist for the Rimington Trophy. The list of Wuerffel winners shows Ikard as the program's first, with Ty Darlington following in 2015.
